# Corey Tate

# Google Nano Banana 2.1 just got better at the stuff that matters.

### Get the updates that matter.

Corey Tate

The new image model brings stronger subject consistency, better mask-based editing, sharper visual design, and improved text rendering; making it more useful for iterative creative work rather than one-shot image generation.

The biggest upgrade may be control: you can make targeted edits while preserving the parts of an image you want to keep, while multi-image reference support can maintain consistency across characters and objects.

And Google is already putting it inside AI Mode in Search, making the model available in a place far beyond the Gemini app.

The image-generation race is increasingly becoming an editing-and-control race.

results.content:
Nano Banana 2.1 still has room for several quality improvements:

 Poor text rendering in small text (often blurry in 1k model), long paragraphs, page length
 Character consistency is not always perfect between input images and generated output image
 Partial instruction following and ink persistence in masked/doodle based editing
 During image editing, we observe rare instances of persistent subject pose, where structural alignment from the input image is retained in the generated output image
 Occasional confusion around spatial localisation (e.g. left/right etc.)
 Still limited in advanced capabilities with world knowledge, 3D reasoning and factuality [...] Capabilities: Editing

### Benefit and Intended Usage

Nano Banana 2.1 is capable of using Gemini’s real-world knowledge to deliver precise results and reflect the world around you, from complex infographics to historically accurate scenes. It is well-suited for applications that require:

 creation and editing of images with professional levels of precision and control and multiple, quick iterations
 generation of clear text for posters and intricate diagrams
 long context real-world knowledge
 localized text rendering across several languages

### Known Limitations

Nano Banana 2.1 may exhibit some of the general limitations of foundation models, such as hallucinations. There may also be occasional slowness or timeout issues.

According to Google, version 2.1 improves visual quality, text rendering, character consistency across conversation turns, wide panoramas, and infographics. It can process up to 14 reference images at once, keeping up to four characters and ten objects consistent. The model also connects to Google Search and offers minimal, medium, and high thinking levels that affect image quality.

Ad [...] It replaces Nano Banana 2, released in February 2026, and Google says it improves on previous versions "across the board." Nano Banana Pro likely remains Google's best image model, but it uses the most recent Pro model, 3.1, while 2.1 uses Gemini 3.6 Flash. The next major gain in image quality could come with Google's announced Pro model, Gemini 4 Argon.

Google is also cutting prices roughly in half compared with Nano Banana 2. A 1K image costs 3.36 cents, down from 6.70 cents, while a 4K image drops from 15.10 to 7.56 cents. Nano Banana Pro costs considerably more at 13.40 cents per 1K image.
